mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals a loosening of monetary policy, which typically leads to increased liquidity in the market and higher S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances when FEDFUNDS decreases by > 0.25%.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) indicates a strengthening labor market, which boosts consumer confidence and spending, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 forward 5-day returns are negative in more than 55% of the instances when PAYEMS increases.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in real estate sales (HOUST) suggests increased demand in the housing market, which is a leading indicator of economic growth and thus positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are negative in more than 45% of the instances when HOUST increases by > 5% YoY.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) signals a contraction in the supply side of the economy, which can lead to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate earnings are expected to decline.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances when INDPRO decreases by > 1% MoM.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) coupled with a decrease in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) indicates a weakening labor market, which can lead to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer spending is expected to decline.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE increases by > 0.2% and PAYEMS decreases by > 100,000
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of the instances when UNRATE and PAYEMS meet the trigger conditions.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in retail sales (RSAFS) combined with a decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) suggests a strengthening consumer sector, which can lead to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS increases by > 2% MoM and UNRATE decreases by > 0.1%
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are negative in more than 45% of the instances when RSAFS and UNRATE meet the trigger conditions.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) without a corresponding increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) suggests inflationary pressure without monetary tightening, which can lead to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as real returns are eroded.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL increases by > 0.5% MoM and FEDFUNDS remains unchanged
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances when CPIAUCSL and FEDFUNDS meet the trigger conditions.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in GDP (GDPC1) combined with a decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) indicates a broad-based economic contraction, which can lead to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings are expected to decline.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 decreases by > 1% QoQ and INDPRO decreases by > 1% MoM
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of the instances when GDPC1 and INDPRO meet the trigger conditions.
